title: Sepsis One-Hour Bundle: Strict Boundaries and Exclusions

numbers.context: Max delay for blood cultures before antimicrobials
Antimicrobials window for septic shock or likely sepsis
Diagnostic window only if sepsis possible without shock; fluid window
Balanced crystalloids within 3 h for hypoperfusion
IV hydrocortisone only for refractory septic shock
Bicarbonate exception threshold with AKI stage 2-3

negations.phrase: never delay antimicrobial administration by more than 45 minutes while waiting for cultures
negations.rule: Cultures must never delay antibiotics >45 min

negations.phrase: Do not add empiric antifungal coverage unless the patient has high fungal risk factors
negations.rule: No empiric antifungals unless high fungal risk

negations.phrase: do not continue dual Gram-negative therapy once susceptibilities are known except in resistant pathogens where monotherapy is inadequate
negations.rule: Stop dual Gram-negative therapy once susceptibilities known unless resistant

negations.phrase: Do not use hydroxyethyl starches under any circumstance
Do not rely on central venous pressure alone to guide fluid responsiveness
negations.rule: Never rely on CVP alone for fluid responsiveness

negations.phrase: Do not withhold vasopressors while waiting to complete the 30 mL/kg fluid bolus if life-threatening hypotension (MAP <65 mmHg) persists
negations.rule: Start vasopressors early if MAP <65 persists; do not wait for full 30 mL/kg

negations.phrase: Never use dopamine unless the patient has symptomatic bradycardia with a low risk of tachyarrhythmias
negations.rule: No dopamine unless bradycardic with low tachyarrhythmia risk

negations.phrase: Do not administer intravenous hydrocortisone (200 mg/day) routinely in sepsis without shock
negations.rule: No routine steroids in sepsis without shock

negations.phrase: Do not give sodium bicarbonate to improve haemodynamics or reduce vasopressor requirements in hypoperfusion-induced lactic acidaemia unless arterial pH is ≤7.15 with acute kidney injury (AKIN stage 2 or 3)
negations.rule: No bicarbonate unless pH ≤7.15 with AKI stage 2-3

conditions.phrase: only if sepsis is possible without shock
conditions.rule: 3-hour window applies only when sepsis is possible without shock

conditions.phrase: unless the patient has high fungal risk factors
only while central venous access is being obtained
conditions.rule: Peripheral norepinephrine is temporary only while obtaining central access

conditions.phrase: unless the patient has symptomatic bradycardia with a low risk of tachyarrhythmias
only for refractory septic shock requiring ongoing vasopressors
unless arterial pH is ≤7.15 with acute kidney injury (AKIN stage 2 or 3)
only when haemoglobin falls below 7.0 g/dL, unless there is active haemorrhage, acute myocardial ischaemia, or severe hypoxaemia

highYield.fact: Cultures before antibiotics, NEVER delaying antibiotics >45 min; IV antibiotics ≤1 h (shock/likely sepsis) vs 3 h ONLY if possible without shock
Balanced crystalloids ≥30 mL/kg within 3 h (lactate ≥4 mmol/L or hypotension); NEVER hydroxyethyl starches; do not rely on CVP alone; do not withhold vasopressors if MAP <65
Norepinephrine first-line (MAP ≥65 mmHg; peripheral only while obtaining central access); vasopressin ≤0.03 U/min ONLY second-line, NEVER first-line
NEVER dopamine unless symptomatic bradycardia + low tachyarrhythmia risk
IV hydrocortisone 200 mg/day ONLY for refractory septic shock, NOT routine without shock
NO sodium bicarbonate unless pH ≤7.15 + AKI (AKIN 2-3); RBC transfusion ONLY if Hb <7.0 g/dL unless haemorrhage, acute MI ischaemia, or severe hypoxaemia
